articleTitle: Improvements to YOLOv4 for Steel Surface Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The effective detection of surface defects in steel is a key concern for steel producers. Conventional target detection algorithms are unable to effectively detect defective targets. Using the advantages of deep learning in feature learning, a surface defect detection algorithm with improved YOLOv4 is proposed to address the problem of poor detection accuracy caused by a variety of steel surface defects and the presence of a large number of small areas and blurred edge damage. Firstly, TBConv (Tied Block Convolution) was introduced to improve the standard convolutional layer in the backbone feature extraction network CSPDarknet to enhance its feature learning capability for different types of surface defects. Secondly, the ECA(Efficient Channel Attention) attention mechanism is introduced in the detection layer to increase the weight of useful features while suppressing the weight of invalid features to improve the ability to fuse shallow and deep information. A cascading bottleneck residual structure is added after the SPP feature pyramid module, with the output of the previous stage being used as the input to the next stage in a sequential training process to enhance the target feature representation. The experimental results show that the improved YOLOv4 algorithm has 6.2% higher accuracy and 27.46% smaller model size compared to the original algorithm, and the algorithm has improved the detection rate of small area defects and can effectively detect surface defect targets.

articleTitle: Underwater Object Detection Based on Improved SSD with Convolutional Block Attention
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: With the ever-increasing demand for marine products with high nutritional value in the sea, rapid and accurate detection of target organisms is highly desired. In this context, a novel underwater object detection algorithm based on improved Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) is proposed to improve the detection accuracy and real-time performance in complex underwater environment. The proposed algorithm employs ResNeXt-50 instead of VGGNet-16 as the backbone network to improve the ability to obtain details and position information of the target object. To be more specific, a channel-spatial attention mechanism is incorporated in the deep layers of the improved XC-SSD model to enhance semantic information of high-level feature maps and reduce missed detection rate and false detection rate. Comprehensive experiments on the URPC-2019 dataset show that the detection accuracy and speed of the proposed algorithm are 79.76% and 18.95 FPS, respectively, which are 3.49% and 2.8 FPS higher than the original SSD algorithm. Experimental results clearly demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is highly efficient and suitable for real-time object detection.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Mobile Robot Navigation in Unknown Environment with Continuous Action Space
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This work aims to propose the use of deep reinforcement learning for mobile robot navigation and obstacle avoidance in previously unknown areas or without pre-made maps with continuous action control to increase the capabilities of mobile robots beyond conventional map-based navigation. Deep reinforcement learning is used to enable the robot to learn how to make decisions and interact with the environment observed from sensor data to safely navigate itself to its destination. The robot has a two-dimensional laser scanner, ultrasonic sensors and odometry sensor. Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient, which can function in continuous action space, was chosen as the deep reinforcement learning model. The robot is trained and tested in a Gazebo simulator with Robot Operating System. After the training process, the robot is put to the challenge to complete a waypoint navigation mission in four unknown areas as part of an assessment. The results indicate that the mobile robot is adaptable and has the capability of traveling to the specified waypoints and completing the job without the need for a pre-drawn route or an obstacle map in unidentified environments with the minimum success rate of 69.7 percent.

articleTitle: An Autonomous Throat Swab Sampling Robot for Nucleic Acid Test
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Throat swab sampling is one of the efficient ways for nucleic acid test. However, the manual sampling work has a high risk of cross-infection, hence the development of autonomous throat swab sampling robot becomes necessary. The design of this kind of machine faces several challenging problems, for instance: (1) it requires coordination of multiple manipulators; (2) it requires an efficient pose calculation algorithm to precisely control the motion of manipulators; and (3) it requires an accurate visual segmentation algorithm to detect the region of interest in the oral cavity. Considering the problems mentioned above, we introduce the prototype of the robot in this paper, which combines multiple manipulators coordination with ma-chine vision technologies. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the robot.

articleTitle: Research on UAV Formation Simulation and Evaluation Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: UAV formation technology will be widely and importantly applied in military and civil fields. In this paper, the formation control strategy was based on the virtual structure method and PID control law. By constructing the hardware-in-the-loop simulation environment and injecting it into a UAV model, it was verified that the formation control strategy and operation logic meet the design requirements. The formation simulation system could achieve the functions of formation assembly, maintenance and transformation, link failure disposal, etc. The evaluation of formation time indicators and distance indicators were achieved by means of a herringbone - diamond - diamond turn simulation profile that verified the rapidity and positional accuracy of the formation. Finally, the evaluation scheme of UAV formation was constructed, which provided users with a comprehensive evaluation method for the performance of UAV. Thus, it provided an important basis for the safe and effective flight test of UAV formation.

articleTitle: High Performance Ship Detection via Transformer and Feature Distillation
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: It has been successfully demonstrated that Transformer is superior in object detection via an encoder-decoder architecture, termed Detection Transformer (DETR). However, slow convergence speed and computational complexity degrade the performance when it is applied to ship detection. The primary reason is ship images are rarely available in large-scale public datasets for training a model. Besides, DETR requires high performance computing platforms to deploy and run, which is not friendly for ship detection application. Towards this end, we propose an Efficient Ship Detection Transformer termed ESDT, which comprises of three parts namely backbone, encoder and decoder. The backbone is implemented with the ResNet50 so that deep features can be extracted. Next, the extracted features are fed to the encoder implemented with multi-scale self-attention to capture the long-range dependency of features. Finally, the enhanced features are sent to the decoder for final ship detection. To speed up converge, we introduce a feature distillation mechanism to the ESDT for learning knowledge from the large pretrained DETR. Extensive experiments are performed on commonly-used ship detection dataset Seaships. Qualitative and quantitative results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Consensus of Linear Singular Multi-agent Systems Based on State Feedback Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In this paper, the consensus problem for singular multi-agent systems is studied with a fixed communication topology consisting of general singular linear dynamics. Based on the local relative state information, a distributed consensus protocol is proposed. It is shown that there exists a consensus protocol solving the consensus problem and meanwhile yielding an unbounded consensus region if and only if each singular agent is both stabilizable and detectable. The Lyapunov theory is used as fundamental tools to establish the stability of the closed-loop system. It is shown that the formation control objective can be achieved if a spanning tree condition is satisfied by the interconnection topology. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are illustrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Underwater Target Detection Based On Modified YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Due to the complex underwater environment, it is not easy to achieve high accuracy of underwater target recognition. To solve this problem, this paper presents a modified YOLOv5s model to improve the accuracy of underwater target detection. Firstly, the number of bottlenecks in the first C3 module of current YOLOv5s is increased from original one to three. Secondly, the Coordinate Attention(CA) module is used to replace the bottleneck module to improve the attention level of the model to the target in the image. Finally, the SE module is embedded in the backbone network of the model to further strengthen the attention of the model, so that the model can concentrate the computing power on the target and ignore the unimportant parts of the image. In the neck network, we make changes to the fusion feature layer. The experimental results show that the improved YOLOv5s model has a 3.7% increase in mAP compared to the original model for the same underwater dataset.

articleTitle: An Improved A* Path Planning Algorithm of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: With the rapid increase in ocean exploration ac-tivities, more and more underwater vehicles for autonomous path planning ability have been designed and developed. There are many limitations on path planning using traditional A* algorithm, such as too many nodes, too many turning times and too small turning angles, and the designed path is not conducive to movement towards autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV). In order to overcome the aforementioned shortcomings, an improved A * algorithm employing path optimization is used to carry out smooth and optimization of the motion path of the AUV. Effectiveness and efficiency optimization of the improved algorithm are verified by simulation studies.

articleTitle: Multi-vehicle Cooperative Confluence Strategy in Freeway Merging Area under New Mixed Traffic Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The continuous development of vehicle intelligence and network technology has promoted the pace of the application of Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) and Connected AVs (CAVs). In the near future, there will be a new traffic situation in which CAVs and human-driven vehicles (HVs) are mixed. In this paper, facing the problem of multi-vehicle confluence in the merging area of freeways under the new mixed traffic environment. On the basis of optimizing the setting of dedicated CAVs lane on the main road, a cooperative confluence model considering ecological driving of vehicles in the merging area is proposed. And the model is verified and analyzed by simulation. The results show that the multi-vehicle cooperative confluence strategy in the freeway merging area proposed in this paper can improve the traffic capacity of the merging area by 5.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, reduce the CO2 emission by 9.6%, and greatly improve the comfort of passengers.

articleTitle: Robot Path Planning Based on Improved Harris Hawk Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In order to obtain better solutions, a global robot path planning method based on the Harris hawk optimization algorithm (HHO) is presented. This method contains two steps, named coarse-grained and fine-grained planning. We construct the environment model based on the MAKLINK graph at first, and then obtain the paths of coarse-grained planning by Dijkstra algorithm. Then two criteria, i.e. path length and smoothness, are considered to evaluate a path, and the mathematical optimization model is established. The HHO algorithm is utilized to solve this mathematic model and complete the final paths of fine-grained planning based on above coarse-grained path planning. Because original HHO algorithm is easy to be stuck into local optima and lacks of balance in exploration and exploitation, the improved Harris hawk optimization algorithm (IHHO) is proposed. In proposed algorithm, a Rank based dynamic update strategy is introduced to update stagnant agents and worse agents, which can ensure the quality and diversity of the population, as well as enhance exploration performance of the algorithm and its ability to jump out of local optima. The proposed algorithm also introduces a nonlinear disturbance control factor into the transition stage of original algorithm, which can effectively balance the exploration and exploitation performances. The presented method is adopted to solve the path planning problem of two robots under two maps with irregular convex obstacles and regular concave obstacles respectively. The simulation results show that obtained paths by IHHO with shorter length and better smoothness, are more superior to those by original HHO. It also verified that presented method is feasible and effective to solve robot path planning problems.

articleTitle: Sonar Image Denoising Based on Anisotropic Guided filtering
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The limitations of imaging principle and imaging environment distort the sonar images by various noises, which causes the sonar image to have the characteristics of low resolution and blurred edges. The existing physical models have certain limitations on the description of sonar noise. In order to adapt to a wider range of sonar images, a filter with blind denoising is the best choice; an edge-preserving filter effectively solves the problem of blurred edges; in real application scenarios, processing efficiency is one of the important factors, and a filter with a linear model has a high processing efficiency. In this paper, the anisotropic guided filter is applied to sonar image denoising. Firstly, the adaptive regularization parameters are obtained using the local variance and the approximate median variance of the natural image. Secondly, the local mean, local variance, and regularization parameters are used to obtain the parameters of the guided filter model. Thirdly, anisotropic weighting is applied to the guided filter model parameters. Finally, the output image is obtained by integrating the anisotropic weighted model parameters with the guidance image. The experiments show that the anisotropic guided filter outperforms the comparison algorithm in the removal of both synthetic and sonar image noise, and achieves efficient sonar image denoising and edge preservation.

articleTitle: Fixed-time Stabilization of Pehlivan System via Adaptive Backstepping Method
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In this paper, the problem of fixed-time control for Pehlivan chaotic system with unknown parameters are investigated. On the basis of the Lyapunov function and fixed-time theory, an adaptive backstepping strategy is presented. The control scheme suppresses the chaotic phenomenon in a fixed time. In the process of design, the unknown parameters are approximated by adaptive control technology, and the piecewise function is proposed to deal with the singular problem appeared in the virtual control law. Simulation results are presented to validate the theory analysis.

articleTitle: Research on Environment Parameter Estimation Based on Regularization Method in RSSI Positioning
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The wireless signal will have a lot of loss in the process of propagation, and there is a certain relationship between the degree of signal loss and the propagation distance. In the indoor positioning algorithm, the Received Signal Strength Indication(RSSI)-based ranging positioning algorithm uses this principle to locate the target. For the ranging algorithm based on RSSI, this paper first improves the model of the algorithm, and then proposes a regularized least squares approach to estimate the unknown parameters <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> in the model. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Distributed Formation Tracking Control of Networked Lagrangian Systems with Collision Avoidance
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In this paper, the formation tracking control problem of networked Euler-Lagrangian (E-L) systems with collision avoidance is considered. A fully distributed control strategy is proposed, in which no global information about the communication topology is required. Furthermore, a potential function is designed to guarantee the collision avoidance. Finally, some numerical simulation results are given to confirm the effectiveness of the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time-Synchronized Consensus Tracking of Multi-agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper investigates the fixed-time-synchronized consensus tracking problem for multi-agent systems with undirected topology. A nonlinear distributed control law for first-order multi-agent systems is proposed based on norm-normalized sign function, with which all the elements of all the agents' states track the leader's state at the same time and in fixed time. Then, the corresponding results are extended to second-order multi-agent systems by adopting the terminal sliding mode control method. Finally, numerical simulations are performed to verify the theoretical results in this paper.

articleTitle: Left-turn Risk Assessment of Autonomous Vehicles at Unsignalized Intersections
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In order to evaluate the interaction risk from surrounding vehicles when an autonomous vehicle turns left at unsignalized intersections, this paper proposes a novel left-turn risk assessment model based on the driving intentions of surrounding vehicles. Naive Bayesian model is employed to predict the driving intention of surrounding vehicles, and the potential spatio-temporal trajectory conflicts among the autonomous vehicle and surrounding vehicles are analyzed based on the separation axis theorem. Then collision risk assessment model is conducted based on the driving intention prediction result of surrounding vehicles as well as the potential conflict metric. An unsignalized intersection simulation scene is built on the Prescan-Simulink simulation platform, and the proposed left-turn risk assessment method is verified. The simulation results indicate that the proposed method can effectively predict the driving intention of other vehicles and assess the interaction risk for autonomous vehicle, especially in the scenario where the driving risks cannot be identified with the method without the safety clearance area.

articleTitle: Path Planning Based on Probabilistic Roadmap and Ant Colony Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In order to handle the path planning problem in complex environments, a novel method combining probabilistic roadmap, ant colony optimization, and third order Bezier curve has been developed in this study. There are three steps in the suggested procedure. Using a probabilistic roadmap approach, a random map is first created based on the complexity of the surrounding area. This could be accomplished by selecting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{N}$</tex> nodes randomly in complex static environments, then establishing connections between these nodes according to specific criteria or conditions. The created roadmap offers a significant number of potential path segments that could link the start and final point. The second stage entails choosing a path within the already-built roadmap. The final path between the start point and the goal point will be searched by using ant colony optimization. Then, the third stage employs a Bezier curve to smooth out and shorten the obtained path. Several simulations in different environments demonstrate that the proposed approach guarantee to obtain a short, smooth, and safe path between the start point and the goal point.

articleTitle: Geometric Collision Avoidance Algorithm for Unmanned Surface Vehicle Based on Multi-objective
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of autonomous collision avoidance when multiple unmanned surface vehicles (USV) meet, and considering the possible existence of abnormally traveling USVs, this paper proposes a distributed collision avoidance algorithm including collision risk detection based on geometric collision avoidance algorithm. First, introduce obstacles Object prediction trajectory and weight factor improve the distance evaluation function of traditional geometric algorithms, and improve the ability of USV to avoid multiple dynamic obstacles. At the same time, a new rule evaluation function is introduced to constrain the USV's avoidance action. Then, the expected speed and heading are improved. The existing collision risk detection algorithm is used to reduce the trajectory fluctuation caused by the change of collision risk. Then, in the process of arriving at the target to distinguish the waypoint, the pure proportional guidance method ensures the safety of the unmanned boat while avoiding intruders. Finally, the simulation verification is carried out in the multi-static and dynamic mixed obstacle scene. The results show that even if there are various dynamic and static obstacles, the geometric collision avoidance algorithm still guarantees the normal USV safe avoidance action.

articleTitle: A Novel Mobile Robot Visual Homing Strategy Based on Pseudo-Isometric Distribution of Landmarks
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Visual homing is an essential technology for robot navigation. However, all landmark-based visual homing methods are usually constrained by the assumption of equal distance of landmarks. To alleviate this assumption, a novel visual homing strategy, termed Pseudo-Isometric Distribution Vector Pre-assigned Mechanism (PD-VPM), is proposed in this paper. The proposed strategy can alleviate effects of randomness and unevenness of landmark distribution. All landmarks can be described by an equivalent representation by adaptively adjusting their weights without artificial interference, so that homing performance is significantly enhanced. Comparative studies demonstrate that the proposed strategy is superior to state-of-the-art methods in terms of homing precision while maintaining computation speed.

articleTitle: Multi-task Cooperative Monocular 3D Object Detection Using Surface Center Keypoints
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Detecting 3D objects from a single monocular image without spatial information is a challenging task. In this paper, we propose a 3D object detection model which directly regresses the center point, depth, size and orientation of the 3D bounding box using a single monocular RGB image. In particular, we obtain multiple surface center points of each 3D box in two ways, one of which is directly predicting them, and the other is indirectly obtaining them through geometry computation. The error between the results in two ways acts as a new unified loss item to improve the convergence of the prediction on surface center points. The proposed approach has been verified on the public nuScenes dataset and experiments demonstrate that the additional keypoints estimation and the unified loss improve some aspects of 3D object detection.

articleTitle: An Advanced Eco-Driving Assistant System for Intelligent Connected Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The rapid development of the automotive industry brings great convenience to people. However, some problems such as fuel consumption, pollutant emissions, and traffic congestion have become more and more serious. Especially in urban freeway, how to solve these problems attracts the attention of researchers. Therefore, with the concept of “carbon peak and carbon neutrality”, this paper designs an advanced eco-driving assistant system for intelligent connected vehicles based on vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication system. Firstly, the intelligent roadside equipment collects traffic and vehicle information in the urban freeway. Secondly, the edge computing server fuses the data to form a holographic perception of dynamic traffic flow and transmits regional road traffic safety warning prompts. At the same time, a minimum energy consumption speed guidance model for vehicles is proposed considering the fused data. Thirdly, an application in V2X communication is designed to display the safety warning prompts, the status of the traffic and vehicles, and the optimal speed guidance. Finally, experimental results from field tests show that the energy consumption of vehicles with the advanced eco-driving assistant system is significantly reduced. In addition, the driver can obtain current traffic status and safety warning prompts, which improves driving safety.

articleTitle: Dual Feedback Based Water Cannon Jet Stabilization System
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In the process of maritime law enforcement by using water cannon, the marine police and marine surveillance ships usually encounter the situation that the vessel shakes due to wind and waves, which leads to the shaking of water cannon and the jet cannot accurately hit the target. The existing water cannon systems mostly adopt the single feedback control method, without considering the interference of the carrier movement on the water jet. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a water cannon jet stabilization system based on dual feedback, using IMU to collect motion pose of carrier, and using autoregressive sliding average model to compensate pose of carrier; using camera to collect information of landing point of water, and using back propagation algorithm to adjust the parameter of jet model in real time and adjust the water cannon joint angle with feedback. The experimental results on the intelligent water cannon platform show that after adopting the dual feedback mechanism, the shooting error of the water jet can be effectively reduced more than 33%.

articleTitle: Auto-DenseNet: DenseNet Optimization Method Based on Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: To address the issue of time-consuming and laborious design of network structure parameters and connection methods, in this paper we propose an evolutionary algorithm-based DenseNet network optimization method (Auto Dense Convolutional Network, Auto-DenseNet). Firstly, the internal parameters of DenseNet are encoded to generate an initial population, and crossover and variation operators are designed to ensure the effectiveness of the evolution of offspring. Secondly, the dataset is imported into the decoded individual evaluation fitness. And then, the superior individuals are selected to enter the next iteration. Finally, the optimized network individuals are selected for the image classification task. After tuning validation on the MNIST-RD dataset, tests were conducted on three widely used benchmark image classification datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that the network structure searched by the Auto-DenseNet algorithm outperforms most existing structures in terms of classification performance, and the number of network parameters.

articleTitle: A Novel Performance Evaluation Method of Ultra-Wideband Positioning System Based on Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper mainly concerns the problem of performance evaluation for an Ultra-Wideband (UWB) positioning system. An evaluation index system suitable for UWB positioning system is established to assess the performance of UWB positioning system from multiple aspects, including accuracy, reliability and anti-interference ability. Analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and entropy weight method (EWM) are combined to yield a more objective weight for each evaluation index. Besides, fuzzy comprehensive evaluation (FCE) is used to conclude the evaluation result. An illustrative example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed evaluation index system and evaluation method.

articleTitle: An Expansion-based Document Ranking Framework Incorporated with Core Concern Capturing
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Entity-based ranking is a popular research area in document ranking as knowledge graphs can introduce additional evidence for ranking systems. In most entity-based ranking framework, the original query is transformed into a set of entities and candidate documents are ranked according to their relevance to the entity set. However, mistakes can easily occur during the transformation process, which introduce noise to the ranking system. This paper represents an expansion-based ranking framework, which expand the original query with high-quality candidate entities to mitigate the impact of transformation mistakes and enrich the semantics of the query in the meanwhile. Compared with existing query expansion methods, our expansion method is lightweight as it reduces much computational burden and requests little extra information. However, the core concerns of the users might be covered up after query expansion. To alleviate this dilemma, a core concern capturing method is pro-posed, wherein the attention weight of each inter-entity relation is measured to capture the core entity pairs in the expanded query. Experiments on the S2-CS dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of our lightweight query expansion method and the superiority of our core concern capturing method. Compared with a classical retrieval model, our method provides 11% improvements in terms of NDCG@15.

articleTitle: Underwater Image Enhancement Based on Improved Haze-lines Prior and Histogram Distribution Prior
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In order to solve the low contrast and color shift suffered by underwater images, a hybrid underwater image enhancement method is proposed in this paper. The global attenuation ratio of the underwater image is calculated by using the background light. Based on this, the transmission map of the underwater image is estimated by using haze-lines prior. Then the clear underwater image is recovered from the degraded underwater image. A contrast enhancement method is introduced further to enrich the color and details. The experimental results on different real-world underwater scenes indicate that the proposed method produces visually satisfactory results.

articleTitle: Marine Object Detection Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The detection of marine objects plays an important role in the exploration and exploitation of marine resources and other marine economic activities. Traditional detection methods are inefficient and low in accuracy. With the development of deep learning, YOLO series algorithms have been widely used in various applications. In this paper, an improved algorithm based on YOLOv5 for maritime object detection has been proposed. The improved algorithm modifies the backbone and neck structure of YOLOv5 through attention mechanism and BiFPN. Experimental results show that our proposed algorithm has superior performances and in particular it obtains better detection results for small objects compared with the original YOLOv5 algorithm. The index of mAP is improved by 1%, and the recall rate is improved by 2%.

articleTitle: Research on Integrated Control of Ship Rudder/ Fin and Main Propulsion Device
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Aiming at the integrated control problem of ship rudder, fin, and main propulsion device, based on the Ship Manoeuvring Mathematical Modeling Group (MMG) modeling method, a four degree of freedom (surging, swaying, rolling and yawing) linearized mathematical model which can truly describe the essence of ship motion is established for a container ship. Using Model Predictive Control (MPC) in dealing with constraint problems, the ship rudder/fin and main propulsion device based on cloud model MPC is designed and verified by simulation. The results show that the integrated control can not only ensure the course and speed under different sea states, achieve a good anti-roll effect, but also reduce the energy consumption, reflecting good adaptability to different sea states.

articleTitle: Improving Seakeeping of Wave-Piercing Catamarans with Flaps Using PID Control
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: High-speed Wave-Piercing Catamarans play an important role in ocean transportation. Due to sharp vertical motion induced by the wave, seakeeping in heaving and pitching motions is invariably affected. To circumvent this problem, a flap, which is a flat plate employed as a hydrofoil to provide lift force in the water flow, is typically installed at the transom stern of each demihull. The strip theory is commonly employed for predicting seakeeping, but the accuracy of prediction is limited by the calculation of flap lift. In order to improve the accuracy of seakeeping prediction, the flaps are no longer considered as an isolated hydrofoil, but a part of the hull, taking into account the effects of transom stern, free water surface and cock-tail wake in this work. Furthermore, a PID controller is successfully designed to control the flaps. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Adaptive Extended State Observer Based Direct Voltage Sliding Mode Control of Stand-Alone DFIG-DC System
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Based on the in-depth analysis of the mathematical model of the doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG), this paper proposes a direct voltage control (DVC) method that combines a high-order adaptive extended state observer and super-twisting sliding mode control for the doubly-fed power generation system. DVC can reduce the number of control variables and sensors, and improve the response speed of the system when dealing with large load disturbances. At the same time, adaptive extended state observer (AESO) adopts a variable gain strategy that is adaptively adjusted according to disturbances, and has both excellent anti-noise and anti-interference capabilities. It combines the advantages of linear extended state observer (LESO) and nonlinear extended state observer (NESO). Finally, simulation prove the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of Path Tracking Control for Wheeled Mobile Robots Based on Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The path tracking control is investigated in this paper using a four-wheeled robot kinematical model and tube-based model predictive control. Simultaneously, in order to improve the robustness, the steering angle calculated by the model predictive controller is converted into the corresponding expected yaw rate through the vehicle kinematical model, owing to the better control effect of the cascade control. To track the expected yaw rate, we use a basic PID controller. By combining the PID controller and the model predictive controller, the path tracking controller bridges the gap between theoretical results and their applications for four-wheeled robot tracking control.

articleTitle: A Novel Generative Adversarial Network for Underwater Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The ocean contains many resources that are vital to the sustainable development of human society. Underwater images provide an important way for people to understand the underwater environment of the ocean. However, due to the uneven medium in water and the scattering effects of light, underwater images usually suffer from some severe degradation problems, such as color distortion and blurring. As such, underwater image enhancement is a very important and critical task in detection of underwater marine objects. To circumvent these problems, a novel generative adversarial network for underwater image enhancement is proposed. In the proposed method, the generator makes use of U-Net network structure and combines CBAM and ASPP to ensure effectiveness of multi-scale feature extraction. The discriminator employs a double-branch structure to guide the generator to generate images from global semantics to local details and enhance local details of the images. Finally, in the quantitative and qualitative analysis, the proposed method is compared with state-of-the-art methods. Comparative studies demonstrate that our proposed method is better than other methods.

articleTitle: Galvanometer Motor Control Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In order to address the problem that the control effect of the galvanometer motor is often dependent on the accuracy of the model parameters, this paper proposes a control method that is based on reinforcement learning. With the galvanometer motor in the steady state as the target, a state feedback control method incorporating an online update control strategy that does not depend on model parameters is proposed on the premise of obtaining the system order, and the method able to identify the state feedback coefficient. As suggested by the computer simulation results, the method proposed in this paper is capable of applying stable control on the galvanometer motor, and the iterative results are found consistent with the design results of the LQR method with the model, which ensures the reliability of the method.

articleTitle: Quantized Adaptive Fault-like Model-based SMC Design for Vehicular Platoon with Actuator Deadzone and Distance Restrictions
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper aims to design an adaptive fault-like model-based sliding-mode control (SMC) law for a class of vehicle platoon systems, where the follower vehicles have quantized input, unknown actuator deadzone, and distance restrictions. Using adaptive terminal sliding mode control method and barrier Lyapunov function (BLF), an adaptive controller is designed to ensure the collision avoidance and communication connection keeping. In addition, the problem of the unknown actuator deadzone and input quantization is first transformed to a fault-like problem, which will simplify the control design procedure. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by a numerical example.

articleTitle: Anti-Disturbance Path Following of Unmanned Surface Vehicles Based on Fuzzy Active Disturbance Rejection Control
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: With the view of achieving path following of unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) in a complex marine environment, a novel path following algorithm based on fuzzy active disturbance rejection control (FADRC) is proposed. Firstly, an improved LOS (IMLOS) guidance law is designed deal with influences of sideslip angle on path following so as to improve robustness of the guidance system. Secondly, to circumvent the problem that the traditional ADRC method cannot automatically adjust system parameters, a FADRC controller which can realize disturbance compensation without accurate model parameters is designed. FADRC can estimate and eliminate internal and external disturbances. The IMLOS and FADRC are integrated to form a composite path following controller. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FADRC.

articleTitle: Group Partition and Group Information based Multi-agent Consensus Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Consensus is a fundamental issue in distributed multi-agent systems, and utilizes the inter-agent relative state to update the state of each agent, so as to achieve global synchronization. Motivated by some scenarios such as privacy-preserving constraints, system measurement error, that the inter-agent relative states are not available, a novel strategy is required to achieve consensus. This paper proposes a consensus algorithm by group partition and state updating via relative group information replacing of the inter-agent relative state. In the scheme, a group of agents are divided into a couple of subgroups by certain probability. This paper proposes a sufficient and necessary condition to reach consensus in mean when subgroup number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m = 2$</tex> and also a sufficient condition when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$m = 2$</tex>. Both numerical simulations and a smart-car hardware platform are provided to demonstrate the validity of our results.

articleTitle: Radar False Alarm Plots Elimination Based on Multi-Feature Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The performance of traditional clutter suppression methods including moving target indication (MTI), moving target detection (MTD) and constant false alarm rate (CFAR) are limited under the background of strong clutter. In order to effectively eliminate false alarm plots caused by clutter, a radar false alarm plots elimination method based on multi-feature evaluation is proposed. Firstly, the density based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) algorithm is used to cluster the radar echo data processed by CFAR. The multi-features including the scale features, time domain features and transform domain features are extracted. Secondly, features evaluation methods are used to evaluate interrelation among features, effective feature combinations are selected as inputs of the classifier. Finally, False alarm plots classified as clutters are eliminated. The experimental results show that proposed method can eliminate about 93% false alarm plots with less target loss rate.

articleTitle: Automatic Charging System for Disinfection Robots Based on Structure-aware Semantic Mapping
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Disinfection robots, which replace human efforts to disinfect the environment, are becoming popular due to the ongoing impact of COVID-19. To address the existing problems of imperfect and costly automatic charging systems for disinfection robots, this paper designs an automatic charging system for disinfection robots based on structure-aware semantic mapping, which optimizes the automatic charging scheme for robots and integrates LIDAR and infrared modules to achieve the goal. Firstly, the data is associated with the charging pile's priori information through structure perception, and the identified semantic information is mapped into the local map of the robot SLAM. Then the infrared module is used to adjust the position of the charging port to align with the charging pile, and TOF laser distance measuring function is also added to avoid damage to the charging pile from the disinfection robot. In 50 times of simulation experiments, our proposed automatic charging system achieves an accurate alignment rate of 96%.

articleTitle: An Event-Triggered Approach to H∞ State Estimation for Neural Networks with Time-Varying Delays
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper investigates event-triggered <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> performance state estimation problem for neural networks model with time-varying delays. A novel event-triggered scheme (ETS) introducing the estimation error is designed, which is a tradeoff between the state estimator performance and network communication bandwidth in accordance with practical requirement. A Wirtinger-type free-matrix-based integral inequality (WFMBII) is put forward, in which some delay-product-type matrices are produced to fully link the relationship among time-varying delay and system states. On these basis, sufficient condition is builded to guarantee the estimation error system to be is bounded and satisfies the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>∞ performance requirement. Meanwhile, the desired event-triggered estimators are solved by linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). A numerical example is given to illustrate the correctness of the obtained method.

articleTitle: A Cloud- Particle-Swarm-Optimization- Backpropagation-Neural-Network- Based Performance Evaluation Method for Cooperative Navigation Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of performance evaluation of cooperative navigation system. Based on the eval-uation needs, a novel evaluation index system is established in this paper. In order to solve the problem of human subjectivity in the evaluation process, this paper proposes a Cloud-Particle-Swarm -Optimization- Backpropagation - N eural- Network evaluation model. The model employs cloud computing to process un-certainty information leveraging Particle-Swarm-Optimization-Backpropagation-Neural-Network evaluation method. Simulation results verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Research on Anti-pursuit Evasion Strategy of Unmanned Surface Vehicle Based on T-D3QN
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: From the perspective of the evader in the pursuit evasion problem of the unmanned surface vehicle (USV), this paper proposes an anti-pursuit evasion strategy for the USV based on Twin-Dueling Double Deep Q Network (T-D3QN), which uses two independent Q networks to estimate the Q value. According to characteristics of the pursuit-evasion problem of the USV, the research designs state space, action space and reward function and constructs the simulation environment to train the model. Simulation experiments show that the performance of T-D3QN is better than DQN because it can improve the escape success rate of the USV, and verify the effectiveness of the evasion strategy for the USV.

articleTitle: Underwater Image Enhancement Based on AttR2U-Net and Multi-Residual Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Underwater optical imaging can intuitively reflect internal state of the ocean. However, due to absorption and scattering of light, the degree of attenuation of different wavelengths of light in seawater is different, and underwater images suffer from low contrast and color distortion. To address the problems, a novel network based on U-Net is proposed for underwater image enhancement in this paper. The network consists of two branches namely Branch1 and Branch2: Branch 1 contains a channel attention module and a recurrent residual convolutional neural network based on spatial attention termed AttR2U-Net that is capable of extracting multiscale features. Branch 2 contains three residual groups, embedded in the residual dense block of the channel attention model, by re-weighting the features of different channels to enhance useful features. Furthermore, through dense cascading and residual learning, convolutional enhancement branches extract high-frequency information such as edges in the corrected image to maintain original structure and edges. Finally, results of the outputs of the two branches are fused. Comparable studies demonstrate that the proposed method is superior to state-of-art methods in color correction on underwater images in different scenes and enhancement of the clarity and contrast of images.

articleTitle: Segmentation of Ship Satellite Images with Transfer Learning and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: As an integrated part of national marine supervision system, ship monitoring plays a critical role in ensuing efficient exploitation of marine resources and safety of territorial sea. In this paper semantic segmentation networks are trained using high-resolution satellite ship data to facilitate more detailed ship inspection. Using the UNet network, the network performance is optimized by improving the structure of the convolutional an attention mechanism is incorporated to enhance useful features and suppress useless features so as to improve segmentation accuracy. The encoder module obtains high-level semantic information of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) remote sensing of ship images layer by layer, and the decoder module recovers spatial information step by step. Experimental results show that this method can effectively enhance accuracy of image segmentation and retain more image details.

articleTitle: Moving Window Non-negative Matrix Projection for Adaptive Process Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: An adaptive process monitoring approach is described for the monitoring of a process with operating condition changes. As a famous dimension reduction technique, non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) has been used in diverse scientific fields including process monitoring since its appearance. However, the existing NMF based monitoring method is only for stationary processes. This paper presents a new variant of NMF called moving window non-negative matrix projection (MWNMP) for monitoring the time-varying processes. The proposed technique incorporates the moving window method into the existing generalized non-negative matrix projection (GNMP) based monitoring for updating the model to reflect the operating mode change. The obtained basis matrix could be updated when the process status changes. Then, the monitoring metrics and the corresponding upper control limits would be recalculated too. The MWNMP based adaptive process monitoring approach is applied to a continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR) process. The monitoring results illustrate the adaptability and feasibility for monitoring the time-varying processes.

articleTitle: Dynamic Inverse Control of Rudder Roll / Yaw Stabilization Based on Rudder Saturation Constraint
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: An adaptive dynamic inverse control method with input constraints was proposed to solve the problem of steering gear saturation caused by large rudder movement in the process of rudder damping. Firstly, the ship roll/yaw system is decoupled into two subsystems according to the different response frequencies of roll and yaw to rudder. Then, the hyperbolic tangent function is used to constrain the actuator input to reduce the amplitude of steering gear and avoid the saturation of steering gear. After that, aiming at the nonlinear, strong coupling and unknown interference characteristics of ship rudder roll/yaw stabilization system, the roll and yaw control rates are designed respectively by nonlinear dynamic inverse control method, the constraint errors and environmental interference are estimated by combining the adaptive law. Finally, the bounded stability of the closed-loop system is proved by constructing Lyapunov function. The simulation results under different sea conditions show that the designed controller not only has good anti-roll effect, but also can effectively reduce the control input and avoid the saturation of steering gear.

articleTitle: Research and Design of 3D Path Obstacle Avoidance Method Between UAVs
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: With the development of high-speed and wide application of UAV technology, at the same time, UAV is faced with more and more complex applications, so its path obstacle avoidance has become a very key problem. One UAV can no longer meet the requirements of the application occasions under the current UAV application background, so the advantages of multiple UAVs are highlighted. UAVs are developing towards the direction of cluster cooperative operation, which is the main development direction of UAVs in the future. UAVs cluster operation means that multiple UAVs communicate with each other to exchange information to achieve coordinated flight, coordinated reconnaissance and coordinated operations. UAV cluster cooperative flight operation must consider the problem of obstacle avoidance between UAVs. Based on the Boid model, this paper proposes a UAV cooperative flight algorithm, and tests the feasibility of the algorithm by using 10 and 20 UAVs in a gradually increasing number based on the 3D test environment. Finally, the simulation results verify that the algorithm has good feasibility in the obstacle avoidance of large-scale UAV 3D cooperative flight between UAVs.

articleTitle: Deflection Motion Characteristics of Magnetically Controlled Capsule Endoscope in an Unstructured Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: To solve the problems of the deflection motion of magnetically controlled capsule endoscopes in an unstructured bending environment, the influence of magnetic induction intensity on the swing characteristics of magnetically controlled capsule endoscopes is analyzed. The magnetic induction intensity model of the master permanent magnet is established to calculate the total magnetic induction intensity of the master permanent magnet at any point in space. The characteristics of the external magnetic field are analyzed, the attitude characteristics and motion trajectory of the capsule endoscope are studied, and the spatial deflection motion characteristics of the capsule endoscope are established. The influence of attitude angle α and β on the fluctuation of the steering process is analyzed, and the relationship between magnetic induction intensity and steering stability is revealed. Simulation analysis shows that the magnetic torque of the capsule endoscope is oscillating attenuated and its oscillation is stable, and the fluctuation of the robot can be effectively suppressed. The research results lay a foundation for the drive of the human intestinal unstructured complex environment.

articleTitle: 6-DoF Occluded Object Semantic Grasp Planning with De-occlusion Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Thanks to previous research, computer vision has now endowed 6-DoF robot arms with the intelligence to plan its best trajectory to a given target. One of the problems that the 6-DoF semantic grasp planning still faces is the solution to grasping occluded targets in a cluttered scene. In such a scenario, the robot arm may not be available to grasp the target in one shot. The current potential attempts to grasp an occluded object include re-arranging the cluttered scene in the hope to expose the target object for a more viable trajectory. However, such methods require multiple viewpoints to model the scene for making global re-arranging plans. Also, the process of re-arranging would take considerable steps to achieve. In our work, we use our decision-making algorithm to combine occlusion prediction (BCNet) with grasp pose planning algorithm (GraspNet), enabling the robot arm to understand the relative positions of each object in a scene. Our method is based on a single viewpoint so that we do not require the robot arm to look all around the scene. In addition, our method is target-motivated, which means we only grasp relevant objects instead of re-arranging all objects in the scene, providing a novel efficient solution to grasp occluded targets.

articleTitle: Helmet Wearing Detection Algorithm Based on Lightweight Network Model
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Aiming at the problems that the traditional helmet wearing detection algorithm has a large amount of parameters and calculation as well as poor real-time performance, which is not conducive to field deployment, helmet wearing detection algorithm called YOLOv4-MAC based on lightweight network model is proposed. Firstly, the YOLOv4 backbone feature extraction network CSPDarkNet53 is replaced by MobileNet V3, and the Depthwise Separable convolution(DW) is used to replace the traditional convolution in PANet and prediction network, which greatly reduces the amount of parameters and calculation; Then SPPNet is replaced by ASPPNet to increase the network receptive field and reduce the amount of network calculation; Finally, CBAM module is added before YOLOHead module to increase the detection ability of small targets. The experimental results show that the mAP of the improved algorithm is 87.82%, the detection speed is greatly improved, and the helmet wearing detection condition can be judged quickly and accurately.

articleTitle: Ship Real-time Route Planning Based on Field Theory and Dynamic Window Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: There are two main problems to be solved in ship real-time route planning. The first problem is how to model the environment of the navigation area, and the second question is how to obtain the optimal action in the current state. In this paper, the dynamic window approach (DWA) is combined with field theory to search the current optimal shipping route. Firstly, the field theory is used to model all obstacles in the environment, which not only considers the size of obstacles, but also highlights the influence of the speed of dynamic obstacles on the path planning. Secondly, the dynamic window method is used to set the search space according to the speed that the ship can achieve in the future period of time to form a dynamic window. Multiple groups of trajectories are generated in the dynamic window, and then evaluated to obtain the optimal trajectory. The simulation results show that the proposed route planning method is effective.

articleTitle: Research on Smoke Detection Model Based on Improved YOLOv4
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of YOLOv4 network in smoke detection, this paper adds the attention module to YOLOv4 and replaces the first downsampling with the Focus module to construct the YOLO-Focus network (abbreviated as YOLO-F in this paper). The addition of the Attention module and Foucs module enables better extraction of smoke information from images, while the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{K}-\mathbf{means}++$</tex> algorithm is used instead of the K-means algorithm to obtain more suitable anchors' size. In order to improve the operation speed of the network in smoke detection devices, a lightweight smoke detection network YOLO-Small (abbreviated as YOLO-S in this paper) is proposed in this paper. In YOLO-S, the number of channels in the network is reduced based on YOLO-F, which makes the network run faster in smoke detection devices. Compared with YOLOv4, YOLO-S has 11.6% higher detection accuracy and 6.69 FPS higher detection rate. Compared with the mainstream lightweight network YOLOv4-mobilenetv3, YOLO-S improves the detection accuracy by 5.4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> while ensuring real-time detection. The comparative experimental results of each network demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed YOLO-S in smoke detection. The comparison experimental results of each network prove the effectiveness of the YOLO-S in the effectiveness of the proposed YOLO-S for smoke detection.

articleTitle: RDCGAN-based Metal Workpieces Image Data Augmentation for Industrial Identification
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The application of deep learning algorithms on various automatic equipment can accomplish many tasks of target detection and identification in industry. Obtaining enough metal workpieces image datasets is a challenge in the real industrial environment. In particular, metal workpieces are vulnerable to lights and other factors. To address this problem, we propose a method for generating metal workpieces images using Restoration Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network (RDCGAN). To improve the quality of the generated images, we integrate an image restoration algorithm. We first design and build the machine vision platform for collecting different kinds of workpieces images in different work conditions. Then we use our RDCGAN to generate metal workpieces images. Finally, we demonstrate that our method produces the images with higher quality compared to the existing approaches in data augmentation methods, as measured by the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID). This approach to metal workpieces image data augmentation can be used in other metal objects data augmentation, to promote the performance of the detection system.

articleTitle: Novel Dynamic Feature Fusion Stragegy for Detection of Small Underwater Marine Object
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Underwater marine object detection has been shown to be significant in the community of marine science and engineering, and has been extensively employed in many practical applications, including commercial fisheries, marine exploration, etc. A typical small object detection trap frequently exists due to the fact that the majority of objects of interest in the underwater environment are usually small. Detection of small marine object is highly desired. This paper presents a novel dynamic feature fusion algorithm based on spatial-aware and scale-aware attention that adaptively fuses different scale feature maps for the detection of small underwater marine objects. Leveraging the proposed dynamic feature fusion algorithm, an improved YOLOX-DFF model is proposed to detect marine organisms in natural seabed environments. To alleviate conflicts between classification and regression tasks in the detection head, the decoupled head of YOLOX-DFF is also augmented with a task-aware attention module. The proposed model surpasses state-of-the-art methods by a large margin of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+0.7mAP$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+2.3AP_{{S}}$</tex> on the DUO dataset. The effectiveness and efficiency of each module are further demonstrated by the ablation studies on PASCAL VOC 0712 datasets, achieving excellent performance with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+1.3mAP$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+3.0AP_{S}$</tex> improvements.

articleTitle: Path Planning of Unmanned Surface Vehicle Port Docking Based on Improved Double Deep Q-Network
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel path planning scheme based on improved Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithm for Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) docking in complex port environment is proposed. First, the port map is pre-processed for edge expansion, and the level of expansion is set according to the complexity of the port environment and the strength of wind. Next, with the view of solving the problem of slow convergence speed and instability of traditional DQN algorithm, an improved Double DQN (DDQN) algorithm with prioritized experience replay and hyperparameter adaptive control is proposed. In order to strike a balance between exploration and exploitation, a dynamic ε scheme is devised to reduce network stabilization time. Finally, the B-spline technique is used to smoothly interpolate the obtained path coordinate points to obtain a viable USV path for port docking. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Human-Like Path Planning for Autonomous Driving Based on Imitation Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In autonomous driving systems, path planning algorithms play a crucial role in ensuring vehicle safety, driving efficiency, and passenger comfort. The traditional path planning algorithms cannot meet the real-time and passenger comfort requirements of autonomous driving, an alternative is imitation learning, a data-driven approach that mimics expert agents' driving behavior and leverages recent advances in supervised learning. We present a learning-based planner that aims to robustly drive a vehicle by mimicking human drivers' driving behavior. First, we leverage a mid-to-mid approach that allows us to reduce sample complexity. Furthermore, we introduce task losses that penalize undesirable behaviors, which is done by introducing a differentiable rasterizer that directly converts the waypoints output by the network into images. Most importantly, we add the state information of ego vehicle at the historical time to the original LSTM network input which improves the completion rate of scene tasks and the comfort of passengers. Finally, we experiment on the nuPlan dataset to verify the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Ship Energy Management Strategy Based on Improved Gravitational Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In order to improve the economy and environmental protection of ship operation, a ship energy management optimization strategy based on gravitation search algorithm (GSA) is proposed. Firstly, the mathematical optimization model of ship energy management is established with the objective of minimizing the operation cost of the ship, considering the relevant performance constraints of diesel engines and generators set, speed limit, arrival time limit and EEOI limit. In addition, considering that the original GSA algorithm has slow convergence speed and is easy to be stuck into local optima, we take some measures and present an improved gravitation search algorithm (IGSA) to overcome them. Function tests show the superior performance of proposed algorithm. Finally, proposed IGSA is adopted to solve above mathematical model, i.e. optimize the power distribution of the operating unit and the sailing speed of the ship. The results of example clearly indicate the benefits from the application of the proposed algorithm and the obtained cost reduction in the ship power system operation. It also shows that proposed IGSA is feasible and effective to the problem of ship energy management strategy.

articleTitle: Data-driven Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Fusion of Multi-direction and Multi-source Signals
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: As a pivotal mechanical component of turbine drive-chain, gearbox suffers from various accidents and fault diagnosis could remarkably enhance its reliability and maintain running safety and lifetime. Vibration-based analysis on single-channel is mainly adopted in previous diagnostic, which cannot catch full vibration inner information in gearbox sensors and bring model performance down. In this paper, a novel method based on the fusion of multi-direction and multi-source signals and the convolutional neural network (MDMS-CNN) is presented. This method can obtain multi-dimensional feature maps from MDMS and preserve the time correlation among different signal sequences. First, features from MDMS are extracted via a corrosion conversion method that converts signals into two-dimensional (2-D) gray images. Then, homologous images are spliced into same channels, while heterogeneous images are superimposed to different channels. Finally, fusion features are input into CNN for fault classification. In experiments, the method is validated on a gearbox diagnosis case. Results have shown that the proposed method achieves 99.86% recognition accuracy and faster convergence speed compared to others.

articleTitle: Operation Parameter Optimization of Cooling Systems in Data Centers Based on NN-HS
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The rapid development of Internet services such as cloud computing has accelerated the construction speed and scale of data centers. High energy consumption has become a prominent problem for data centers. Cooling systems account for a considerable proportion in the total energy consumption of data centers. Operation parameter optimization for reducing energy consumption is one of the key technologies to build green data centers. In order to solve this problem, we propose a new method with PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness) as performance index. Setting the operation parameters of cooling systems as the inputs and the corresponding PUE as the output, the neural network is constructed. The PUE function is approximated by this neural network with historical operating data of the data center of a certain bank in Beijing, and it is taken as the optimization objective. Considering other constraints, the relevant mathematical optimization model is established. At the same time, the harmony search algorithm is improved, including the search method of “seeking advantages and avoiding disadvantages” and the adaptive strategy. Therefore, novel improved harmony search algorithm (IHS) is proposed. Finally, the proposed IHS algorithm is applied to solve the above model. Based on the relevant instance data of the bank, the optimal operation parameters of the cooling system under given conditions are obtained. Through the analysis and comparison of optimal results, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method are verified.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Optimal Trajectory Tracking Control of Underactuated Autonomous Underwater Vehicles Using Double Closed-Loop Control
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In this paper, a double closed-loop control method is proposed for three-dimensional optimal trajectory tracking control of underactuated autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs), Firstly, a five-degree-of-freedom mathematical model of under-actuated AUV is established. Secondly, an output redefinition method is adopted to solve underactuated control problem. On this basis, a backstepping method is utilized to design the outer-loop controller where virtual velocity is derived using the error between input and output of the system. Next, an adaptive dynamic programming method is used to design the inner-loop controller, where the performance index function containing the disturbance upper bound is set, and a neural network is employed to solve the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation online. Finally, the Lyapunov theorem is used to establish that all signals of the closed-loop system are uniformly ultimately bounded. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of Mobile Robot Control System Based on EMG Signal
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In the current research, there are three main control methods for intelligent robot car, which are manual control, remote control and automatic control. And in the field of remote control, whether it is the direct use of remote control or the remote control keys are virtually installed in the mobile phone APP, there is a lack of direct interaction with human. To solve this problem, an intelligent robot car control system was developed to wirelessly control the intelligent car based on electromyography(EMG) signals in this paper. The intelligent robot car responds to the operator's different gestures by moving forward, backward, turning left and turning right. Firstly, EMG signals of different gestures of the forearm are collected, and the collected EMG signals are amplified, filtered and de-noised in MATLAB. Then, the data are processed by corresponding algorithms such as active segment detection, feature extraction and pattern classification on PC to obtain the recognition results of various gestures. Finally, different gestures are analyzed into corresponding commands and the signals are transmitted to the robot car through Bluetooth transmission so as to realize the real-time control of gestures to the robot car motion state. After several experiments, the intelligent car control system based on EMG can effectively control the robot car motion state according to the operator's gesture, and the recognition rate of the selected four gestures is more than 95%, the recognition rate is high, the system performance is good, and has good operability and stability.

articleTitle: A Scenario-Based Model for Analyzing the Ethical Requirements of Intelligent Autonomous Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In this paper, a model for eliciting and analyzing the ethical requirements of an intelligent system is proposed. Considering that intelligent systems are increasingly entering various ethical territories of human life and becoming able to make decisions with ethical consequences, it is suggested that we need to develop guiding models with the perspective that they actively involve requirements engineers in discovering the ethical requirements of such systems during a system's life cycle. In a sense, beyond giving engineers pre-specified ethical standards, engineers themselves, in collaboration with each other and stakeholders, should also be able to iteratively analyze the ethical requirements which are specific to the system under development. A model is better to mainly provide a framework for such a collaborative process. What is suggested in this paper is a scenario-based model of this kind. The effectiveness of scenarios in discovering and specifying a system's requirements has been explored well in the literature. It is argued both how we can use scenarios for ethical purposes in the process of requirements engineering and how philosophical ethical theories can be used in the proposed model by considering, as an example, three influential ethical theories: consequentialism, deontology, and virtue ethics.

articleTitle: A Cooperative Level Curve Tracking Algorithm without Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Algorithms for a multi-robot system to track the desired level curve of a scalar field have a wide range of applications in environmental exploration. Traditional algorithms generally require communications between robots for gradient estimation on the unknown environment. In the case where the accurate global locations and communications are limited, e.g., underwater environments, communication-based algorithms may be inapplicable. This paper proposes an improved algorithm that does not rely on communications nor global locations of robots. A distributed formation control law is designed to solve the level curve tracking problem. Each robot only uses local measurements of the field and relative positions of its neighbors to maintain formation. The dynamics and stability of the algorithm are analyzed. Additionally, the efficiency of the algorithm is validated through simulations.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Map Code Recognition Method
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: For the efficient digitalization of maps, it is neces-sary to register map code, which indicates scale and area range. The manual register of the map code is time-consuming and laborious. Moreover, the recognition accuracy of the traditional text detection method based on template matching cannot be guaranteed. In this study, we propose a deep learning method to recognize image code and solve the problem of inaccurate detection and inaccurate positioning of text areas in map code recognition. A map code target recognition neural network referred to as YOLO-MCRNN is trained first to identify, crop, and binarize the code area and obtain detailed images. Architec-turally, an attention mechanism is added to a bidirectional long short-term memory structure and integrated into the map code target recognition network. Single numbers were cut according to variations in pixel value to establish a template library used in the matching method to recognize the code. Then, we conducted a comparative experiment to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed deep learning method, and the results show that the detection network model improved on the performance of the existing state-of-the-art methods. Recognition experiments were carried out on the image dataset of code images taken by a digital map instrument. The single character and code recognition accuracy of the proposed YOLO-MCRNN model were 0.956 and 0.985, respectively, exhibiting obvious advantages over conventional matching methods and the unimproved text detection model CRNN(Convolutional Neural Network). The YOLO-MCRNN map code recognition network can accurately locate text areas, extract effective deep features of an input image, and identify map code. Compared with CRNN neural networks, which lack regional positioning, YOLO-MCRNN can improve recognition accuracy and reduce time consumption. Thus, the proposed model can be highly effective as an automatic map code registration method.

articleTitle: A Computational Model of MI-EEG Association Prediction Based on SMR-DCT and LS-SVM
publicationTitle: 2022 5th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The theory of feature extraction and pattern classification of Motion Imaging Electroencephalogram (MI-EEG) plays an important role in Brain-computer Interface (BCI) system, which is widely used in rehabilitation medicine, intelligent control and other fields. Although advanced acquisition technologies have generated considerable EEG data for various brain areas, it has inevitable drawbacks such as high cost, time consumption, and inherently high false positive rate of existing methods. In this paper, considering the contradiction between data quantity and accuracy, we used a two-step feature extraction method based on Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) together with Least Squares Support Vector Machine (LS-SVM) to perform feature extraction and classification for single-trial MI EEG. Based on the dataset constructed from the Project BCI-EEG motor activity, the average ACC, PE, SN and MCC of seven channels in the central and temporal lobes of the brain are 90.27%, 91.28%, 89.35%, and 82.34% were obtained with 5-fold cross validation, respectively. Furthermore, the same method was applied to the BCI Competition IV dataset, and the above results were also confirmed. The performance comparison with previous prediction models show that our method used fewer channels, but the accuracy was higher and more reliable. It is anticipated that the proposed method can be used as an effective computational tool for future BCI researches.
